summary: Flathead NF cabin built 1928 on Coal Ridge, still standing as the Moran Patrol Cabin; the 1935 L-4 tower beside it is in ruins; reached by hiking Trail 2.

facts.status_note: The 1928 cabin still stands; the 1935 L-4 tower is in ruins, with part of them still standing

access.note: Hike on Forest Service Trail 2 from the Moran Basin Road trailhead; a North Fork Trails report describes road slides that had been cut out only days before. No closure found.

visit.trail_note: About 6.8 miles round trip from the Moran Basin Road trailhead to the ridgetop (North Fork Trails hike report)

events.note: Cabin at the northwest point of the ridge; also called the Moran Patrol Cabin
20-foot pole L-4 tower about a mile southeast of the cabin; Montana Lookouts gives 24 feet
Used for emergencies in the 1960s; the source gives only the decade
Forest Service crews installed new siding on the cabin; the North Fork post links the work to the Northwest Montana Lookout Association's 2014 projects page. The post gives no year of its own.

corrections.why: NHLR says the 1928 cabin is still there. The firelookout.org 'Tower Gone' label fits the 1935 tower, which is in ruins, not the cabin.
The L-4 design belongs to the 20-foot pole tower built in 1935, not to the 1928 cabin that the record describes. These sources give no design for the cabin.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Firelookout.com give the 1935 L-4 tower as 20 feet, which is the record's 6.1 m; Montana Lookouts gives 24 feet.
Firelookout.org labels the site 'Tower Gone' while NHLR says the cabin is still there. The tower is in ruins, so both can be true.

notes_for_editor: Record says status gone, design L-4, height 6.1 m, access unknown. NHLR says the 1928 cabin is still there, so status and design were corrected; kind 'tower' fits the 1935 tower rather than the cabin, editor to decide. Not verified: the 2012-2014 rehabilitation and the 2016 paint and 2017 gable and wall work from the existing record. The NWMT 2014 and 2017 project pages were not readable (the 2017 page is a PDF wrapper), so those events are left out. The 2014 date rests on the North Fork post's link to the 2014 projects page. The 1930s platform tower has no year in the sources, so it is not an event. Access 'public' is inferred from the national forest trail route; trail details are from an older hike report, so check current road and trail status. The NHLR coordinate sits at 7,268 ft, between the cabin (7,285 ft) and the 1935 tower (7,105 ft). No new photos added.
